2. Load packages, examine, and filter data
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

str(fluid.data)

# Right now, there are only 3 columns relevant to analysis (germinate, lytic.event, MOI)
table(fluid.data$germinate, useNA = "ifany")

table(fluid.data$lytic.event, useNA = "ifany")

table(fluid.data$MOI, useNA = "ifany")

# Subset out the data that we are currently interested in working with (spore, germinate, time.germinate, lytic.event, MOI, series, batch, infected.control)
fluid.sub <- fluid.data %>%
  select(
    spore,
    germinate,
    time.germinate,
    lytic.event,
    MOI,
    series,
    batch,
    Infected.control
  )

glimpse(fluid.sub)


table(
  fluid.sub$Infected.control,
  fluid.sub$MOI,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

# Filter data for treatments of interest
fluid.filtered <- fluid.sub %>%
  filter(
    Infected.control == "control" |
    (Infected.control == "infected" & MOI == 1)
  )
# verify
table(
  fluid.filtered$Infected.control,
  fluid.filtered$MOI,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

# For now, only include spores with definitive germination outcome
fluid.germ <- fluid.filtered %>%
  filter(germinate %in% c("0", "1"))

# verify 
table(
  fluid.germ$Infected.control,
  fluid.germ$germinate
)
```
3. Initial analysis (given that we only have data for 1 rep for each treatment, we can't push our analysis too far just yet)
```{r}
# Subset germinated spores with definitive lysis outcomes
fluid.lysis <- fluid.filtered %>%
  filter(
    germinate == "1",
    lytic.event %in% c("0", "1")
  )


# Calculate percentage lysis per microscope position
lysis_summary <- fluid.lysis %>%
  group_by(Infected.control, batch, series) %>%
  summarise(
    total_germinated = n(),

    total_lysed = sum(lytic.event == "1"),

    percent_lysis = 
      (total_lysed / total_germinated) * 100,

    .groups = "drop"
  )


lysis_plot <- ggplot(
  lysis_summary,
  aes(
    x = Infected.control,
    y = percent_lysis,
    fill = Infected.control
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.6,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.08,
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "control" = "#4C78A8",
      "infected" = "#C44E52"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Lysis (% of germinated spores)"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )
lysis_plot
```

####### PART  2: MODEL FITTING ##########
- We will start off by testing control (uninfected spores) and infected spores separately for model fits
- We aim to test the following models: Weibull, Logistic, Log logistic, Erlang, Discrete Bernoulli 
- We want to know: What probability distribution best describes time to germination? 
- Do infected and uninfected spores exhibit different germ time distributions?
- What biological info can we extract from fitted models? 

1. Starting only with control spores 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

control_data <- fluid.data %>%
  filter(
    Infected.control == "control",
    germinate == 1,
    !is.na(time.germinate)
  )

# Inspect germination times
summary(control_data$time.germinate)

hist(
  control_data$time.germinate,
  breaks = 30,
  main = "Control spore germination times",
  xlab = "Time to germination (minutes)"
)

# Examine times
summary(control_data$time.germinate)

table(control_data$time.germinate)
```
Weibull pre-check
```{r}
probabilities <- pweibull(
  upper,
  shape = 2,
  scale = 16
) -
  pweibull(
    lower,
    shape = 2,
    scale = 16
)

# How many probabilities are zero?
sum(probabilities == 0, na.rm = TRUE)

# Which observations have invalid probabilities?
data.frame(
  time = times,
  lower = lower,
  upper = upper,
  probability = probabilities
) %>%
  filter(
    is.na(probability) | probability <= 0
  )
```



2. Weibull
- the Weibull distribution is a continuous probability distribution commonly used to model time to event data 
- Unlike the normal distribution, Weibull is defined only for nonnegative times and can accommodate right-skewed observations
- It has two parameters: shape (k) and scale (lambda)
- The shape parameter controls how the instantaneous event rate, called the hazard, changes with time
- The scale parameter controls the timescale over which germination occurs (larger scale means longer germ times)
- Because our germination data is recorded every 2 min, we are interested in the probability of germination within a particular interval
```{r}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(bbmle)
# Extract germination times 
times <- control_data$time.germinate

summary(times)

# Check germination times 
summary(times)

sum(is.na(times))
sum(!is.finite(times))
sum(times == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(times < 0, na.rm = TRUE)

# We do have a single time of germination as 0 
# Define observation interval
library(bbmle)

# Observation interval
dt <- 2

# Define interval boundaries
upper <- ifelse(times == 0, dt, times)
lower <- pmax(0, upper - dt)

# Define negative log liklihood
weibull_nll <- function(shape, scale) {

  if (shape <= 0 || scale <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  # Log survival at each interval boundary
  log_S_lower <- pweibull(
    lower,
    shape = shape,
    scale = scale,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- pweibull(
    upper,
    shape = shape,
    scale = scale,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  # Stable log interval probabilities
  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower +
    log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}

weibull_nll(shape = 2, scale = 16)

# Fit Weibull using MLE
weibull_fit <- mle2(
  weibull_nll,
  start = list(
    shape = 2,
    scale = median(times)
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    shape = 0.001,
    scale = 0.001
  )
)

# Results
summary(weibull_fit)

coef(weibull_fit)

AIC(weibull_fit)
BIC(weibull_fit) #BIC returns NA, let's calculate manually below
weibull_fit@details$convergence # 0 

# Calculating BIC
n <- length(times)

logLik_value <- as.numeric(logLik(weibull_fit))

k <- length(coef(weibull_fit))

BIC_weibull <- -2 * logLik_value + k * log(n)

BIC_weibull
```
- Because the shape parameter here (k) = 0.805, the instantaneous germination hazard decreases among spores that have not yet germinated
# Plot Weibull
```{r}
ggplot(control_data, aes(x = time.germinate)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    binwidth = 2,
    fill = "grey80",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  stat_function(
    fun = dweibull,
    args = list(
      shape = coef(weibull_fit)["shape"],
      scale = coef(weibull_fit)["scale"]
    ),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time to germination (min)",
    y = "Probability density",
    title = "Weibull fit to control spore germination times"
  )

# Plot Weibull 
# Extract fitted Weibull parameters
weibull_params <- coef(weibull_fit)

# Create 2-minute intervals
plot_times <- seq(
  0,
  max(times) + 2,
  by = 2
)

# Calculate predicted probabilities for each interval
weibull_predictions <- data.frame(
  time = plot_times[-1]
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_prob =
      pweibull(
        time,
        shape = weibull_params["shape"],
        scale = weibull_params["scale"]
      ) -
      pweibull(
        time - 2,
        shape = weibull_params["shape"],
        scale = weibull_params["scale"]
      ),
    predicted_count = predicted_prob * length(times)
  )

# Observed counts
observed_counts <- data.frame(
  time = ifelse(times == 0, 2, times)
) %>%
  count(time, name = "observed_count")

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = observed_counts,
    aes(x = time, y = observed_count),
    width = 2,
    fill = "grey75",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = weibull_predictions,
    aes(x = time, y = predicted_count),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Weibull fit to control germination times",
    x = "Time to germination (minutes)",
    y = "Number of spores"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100))
```
3. Logistic 
- Logistic has two parameters: location (u) which determines where the distribution is centered and scale (s) controls how spread out the germiation times are. 
- we are fitting the model using interval probabilities here 
- the ordinary logistic distribution is not necessarily well suited for time to event data because it allows negative values
- the logistic distribution is a continuous probability distribution that resembles the normal distributuon (symmetric, bell shaped, heavier tails)

```{r}
logistic_nll <- function(location, scale) {

  if (scale <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  log_S_lower <- plogis(
    lower,
    location = location,
    scale = scale,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- plogis(
    upper,
    location = location,
    scale = scale,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower +
    log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}

# Fit the logistic distribution
logistic_fit <- mle2(
  logistic_nll,
  start = list(
    location = median(times),
    scale = sd(times) / 2
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    location = -Inf,
    scale = 0.001
  )
)
summary(logistic_fit)
coef(logistic_fit)
AIC(logistic_fit)
BIC(logistic_fit)
logistic_fit@details$convergence

# Calculate BIC manually since we get NA 

n <- length(times)

BIC_logistic <- -2 * as.numeric(logLik(logistic_fit)) +
  length(coef(logistic_fit)) * log(n)

BIC_logistic
```

# Plot logistic
```{r}
# Extract fitted logistic parameters
logistic_params <- coef(logistic_fit)

# Create 2-minute intervals
plot_times <- seq(
  0,
  max(times) + 2,
  by = 2
)

# Calculate predicted probability for each interval
logistic_predictions <- data.frame(
  time = plot_times[-1]
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_prob =
      plogis(time,
             location = logistic_params["location"],
             scale = logistic_params["scale"]) -
      plogis(time - 2,
             location = logistic_params["location"],
             scale = logistic_params["scale"]),
    predicted_count = predicted_prob * length(times)
  )

# Observed counts
observed_counts <- data.frame(
  time = ifelse(times == 0, 2, times)
) %>%
  count(time, name = "observed_count")

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = observed_counts,
    aes(x = time, y = observed_count),
    width = 2,
    fill = "grey75",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = logistic_predictions,
    aes(x = time, y = predicted_count),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Logistic fit to control germination times",
    x = "Time to germination (minutes)",
    y = "Number of spores"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100))
```
4. Log logistic 
- log logistic distribution can describe a germination hazard that initially increases and then decreases (which is most consistent with observed data)
- log logistic distribution is a continuous probability distribution used to model positive-values time to event data 
- this is useful to test because we have non-negative times, strongly right skewed data, and a long tail 
- It contains two parameters: shape (alpha) controls the shape of the distribution and how the hazard changes over time, 
scale (beta) determines the timescale and equals the median germination time
- in this case the hazard means the instantaneous germination rate among spores that have not yet germinated
- Important to keep in mind here: the dataset only contains spores that have germinated, and so the fitted distributions describe germination timing among observed germinators, not the probability that any spore will eventually germinate
```{r}
# Define function
loglogistic_nll <- function(shape, scale) {

  if (shape <= 0 || scale <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  log_S_lower <- plogis(
    log(lower),
    location = log(scale),
    scale = 1 / shape,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- plogis(
    log(upper),
    location = log(scale),
    scale = 1 / shape,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower +
    log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}

# Fit 
loglogistic_fit <- mle2(
  loglogistic_nll,
  start = list(
    shape = 2,
    scale = median(times)
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    shape = 0.001,
    scale = 0.001
  )
)

summary(loglogistic_fit)

coef(loglogistic_fit)

AIC(loglogistic_fit)

loglogistic_fit@details$convergence

# Caculate BIC manually 
n <- length(times)

BIC_loglogistic <-
  -2 * as.numeric(logLik(loglogistic_fit)) +
  length(coef(loglogistic_fit)) * log(n)

BIC_loglogistic
```

```{r}
# Log-logistic CDF
pllogis <- function(t, shape, scale) {

}

# Plot
ggplot() +
```

5. Erlang
- continuous probability distribution used to model the time required for a specified number of events or stages to occur
- special case of the gamma distribution in which the shape parameter must be a positive integer
- two parameters: shape (k) and rate (lamba)
```{r}
# Define function
erlang_nll <- function(rate, shape) {

  if (rate <= 0 || shape < 1 || shape != floor(shape)) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  log_S_lower <- pgamma(
    lower,
    shape = shape,
    rate = rate,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- pgamma(
    upper,
    shape = shape,
    rate = rate,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower + log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}

# Fit 
library(bbmle)

erlang_fits <- lapply(1:20, function(k) {

  mle2(
    erlang_nll,
    start = list(rate = k / mean(times)),
    fixed = list(shape = k),
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = c(rate = 0.000001)
  )

})

# Results
erlang_results <- data.frame(
  shape = 1:20,
  rate = sapply(erlang_fits, function(fit) {
    unname(coef(fit)["rate"])
  }),
  logLik = sapply(erlang_fits, function(fit) {
    as.numeric(logLik(fit))
  })
) %>%
  mutate(
    AIC = -2 * logLik + 4,
    BIC = -2 * logLik + 2 * log(length(times))
  )

erlang_results
```
# Identify the best fitting erlang and plot

```{r}
best_index <- which.min(erlang_results$AIC)

best_erlang <- erlang_fits[[best_index]]

best_shape <- erlang_results$shape[best_index]
best_rate <- erlang_results$rate[best_index]

best_shape
best_rate

# Define 2-minute time intervals

# Calculate predicted counts
erlang_predictions <- data.frame(
  time = plot_times[-1]
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_prob =
      pgamma(
        time,
        shape = best_shape,
        rate = best_rate
      ) -
      pgamma(
        time - 2,
        shape = best_shape,
        rate = best_rate
      ),

    predicted_count = predicted_prob * length(times)
  )

# Plot observed vs predicted germ times
# Observed counts

  time = ifelse(times == 0, 2, times)
) %>%
  mutate(time = 2 * ceiling(time / 2)) %>%

# Plot

  geom_col(

  ) +

    data = erlang_predictions,
    aes(x = time, y = predicted_count),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

    title = "Erlang fit to control germination times",

erlang_plot +
```

6. Discrete Bernoulli 
- this is not continuous -- instead we will be dividing the experiment into 2 min intervals and during each interval there are two possibile outcomes 
- We are actually going to use the geometric distribution (becasue we are only dealing with spores that have germinated)
- SO, each 2 min interval is treated as a bernoulli trial, germination occurs with probability p
```{r}
# Germination times
dt <- 2

intervals <- pmax(1, ceiling(times / dt))

head(data.frame(
  time = times,
  interval = intervals
))

# define geometric 
geometric_nll <- function(p) {

  if (p <= 0 || p >= 1) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(
    log(p) +
    (intervals - 1) * log1p(-p)
  )
}

# Fit 
library(bbmle)

geometric_fit <- mle2(
  geometric_nll,
  start = list(p = 0.05),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(p = 0.000001),
  upper = c(p = 0.999999)
)
# Results 
summary(geometric_fit)

coef(geometric_fit)

AIC(geometric_fit)

geometric_fit@details$convergence

# Manually calculate BIC
n <- length(intervals)

BIC_geometric <-
  -2 * as.numeric(logLik(geometric_fit)) +
  log(n)

BIC_geometric
```
Plot 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

p_hat <- unname(coef(geometric_fit)["p"])

geometric_predictions <- data.frame(
  interval = 1:max(intervals)
) %>%
  mutate(
    time = interval * dt,
    predicted_prob = dgeom(interval - 1, prob = p_hat),
    predicted_count = predicted_prob * length(intervals)
  )

observed_counts <- data.frame(
  interval = intervals
) %>%
  count(interval, name = "observed_count") %>%
  mutate(time = interval * dt)

geometric_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = observed_counts,
    aes(x = time, y = observed_count),
    width = 2,
    fill = "grey75",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = geometric_predictions,
    aes(x = time, y = predicted_count),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Geometric fit to control germination times",
    x = "Time to germination (minutes)",
    y = "Number of spores"
  ) 

geometric_plot +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100))
```
7. Lognormal 
- The lognormal distribution assumes that the data follows a normal distribution 
- It contains two parms: (u) meanlog--the mean of log-transformed germination times and (o (theta)) sdlog, the standard deviation of the log-transformed germination times 
- The log normal distribution is right skewed, which agrees with our observed data, it can also accomodate long tails

# Define interval boundaries
```{r}
# Control germination times
times_control <- times

# Define 2-minute intervals
upper_control <- ifelse(times_control == 0, 2, times_control)
lower_control <- pmax(0, upper_control - 2)

# Define negative log-liklihood
library(bbmle)

lognormal_nll_control <- function(meanlog, sdlog) {

  if (sdlog <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  log_S_lower <- plnorm(
    lower_control,
    meanlog = meanlog,
    sdlog = sdlog,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- plnorm(
    upper_control,
    meanlog = meanlog,
    sdlog = sdlog,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower +
    log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}

# Fit using MLE
# Starting values based on positive germination times
log_times <- log(times_control[times_control > 0])

lognormal_fit_control <- mle2(
  lognormal_nll_control,
  start = list(
    meanlog = mean(log_times),
    sdlog = sd(log_times)
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    meanlog = -Inf,
    sdlog = 0.001
  )
)

summary(lognormal_fit_control)

coef(lognormal_fit_control)

AIC(lognormal_fit_control)

BIC(lognormal_fit_control)

lognormal_fit_control@details$convergence

# Manually calculate BIC
n_control <- length(times_control)

BIC_lognormal_control <-
  -2 * as.numeric(logLik(lognormal_fit_control)) +
  length(coef(lognormal_fit_control)) * log(n_control)

BIC_lognormal_control
```

# Calculate the median germination time based on model
```{r}
median_lognormal_control <-
  exp(coef(lognormal_fit_control)["meanlog"])

median_lognormal_control
```

# Plot
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Observed counts
observed_counts_control <- data.frame(
  time = upper_control
) %>%
  count(time, name = "observed_count")

# Fitted parameters
mu <- coef(lognormal_fit_control)["meanlog"]
sigma <- coef(lognormal_fit_control)["sdlog"]

# Predicted counts
lognormal_predictions_control <- data.frame(
  time = seq(2, max(upper_control), by = 2)
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_prob =
      plnorm(time, meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma) -
      plnorm(time - 2, meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma),

    predicted_count =
      predicted_prob * length(times_control)
  )

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = observed_counts_control,
    aes(x = time, y = observed_count),
    width = 2,
    fill = "grey75",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = lognormal_predictions_control,
    aes(x = time, y = predicted_count),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Log-normal fit to control germination times",
    x = "Time to germination (minutes)",
    y = "Number of spores"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100))
```

```{r}
library(bbmle)
library(dplyr)
loglogistic_nll_viro <- function(shape, scale) {

  if (shape <= 0 || scale <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  log_S_lower <- plogis(
    log(lower_viro),
    location = log(scale),
    scale = 1 / shape,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- plogis(
    log(upper_viro),
    location = log(scale),
    scale = 1 / shape,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower +
    log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}
```

4. Generalized gamma 
- this distribution has 3 parms: mu which is the location parameter on the log-time scale
- sigma which controls the spread of germination times
- Q which controls the distributional shape and skewness (when Q = 0, the gamma reduces to the log-normal distribution)
# Install package for gamma 
```{r}
library(flexsurv)
library(bbmle)
```
# Define the generalized gamma negative log-liklihood
```{r}
gengamma_nll_viro <- function(mu, sigma, Q) {

  if (sigma <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  log_S_lower <- pgengamma(
    lower_viro,
    mu = mu,
    sigma = sigma,
    Q = Q,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- pgengamma(
    upper_viro,
    mu = mu,
    sigma = sigma,
    Q = Q,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower +
    log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}
```


# Fit and examine
```{r}

    Q = 0.1
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    mu = -Inf,
    sigma = 0.001,
    Q = -10
  ),
  upper = c(
    mu = Inf,

    Q = 10

)
```

5. Ex-Gaussian
- 3 parameters: mu which is the location of the Gaussian component, sigma which is the standard deviation of the Gaussian component and then tau, which is the exponential component and controls the extended right tail 
```{r}
pexgauss <- function(x, mu, sigma, tau) {

  z <- (x - mu) / sigma

  pnorm(z) -
    exp(
      -(x - mu) / tau +
      sigma^2 / (2 * tau^2)
    ) *
    pnorm(z - sigma / tau)
}

# Define the negative log liklihood
library(bbmle)

exgauss_nll_viro <- function(mu, sigma, tau) {

  if (sigma <= 0 || tau <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  F_lower <- pexgauss(
    lower_viro,
    mu = mu,
    sigma = sigma,
    tau = tau
  )

  F_upper <- pexgauss(
    upper_viro,
    mu = mu,
    sigma = sigma,
    tau = tau
  )

  prob <- F_upper - F_lower

  if (any(!is.finite(prob)) || any(prob <= 0)) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log(prob))
}

# Fit

exgauss_fit_viro <- mle2(
  exgauss_nll_viro,
  start = list(
    mu = 5,
    sigma = 3,
    tau = 15
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    mu = -100,
    sigma = 0.01,
    tau = 0.01
  ),
  upper = c(
    mu = 100,
    sigma = 100,
    tau = 1000
  )
)

summary(exgauss_fit_viro)
# Check convergence
exgauss_fit_viro@details$convergence

# AIC and BIC
AIC(exgauss_fit_viro)

BIC_exgauss_viro <-
  -2 * as.numeric(logLik(exgauss_fit_viro)) +
  length(coef(exgauss_fit_viro)) * log(length(times_viro))

BIC_exgauss_viro
```

# Define the shared log-logistic liklihood
```{r}
loglogistic_nll_shared <- function(shape, scale) {

  if (shape <= 0 || scale <= 0) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  log_S_lower <- plogis(
    log(lower_combined),
    location = log(scale),
    scale = 1 / shape,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  log_S_upper <- plogis(
    log(upper_combined),
    location = log(scale),
    scale = 1 / shape,
    lower.tail = FALSE,
    log.p = TRUE
  )

  delta <- log_S_upper - log_S_lower

  log_prob <- log_S_lower +
    log(-expm1(delta))

  if (any(!is.finite(log_prob))) {
    return(1e100)
  }

  -sum(log_prob)
}
```

# Fit shared parameter model
```{r}
library(bbmle)

loglogistic_fit_shared <- mle2(
  loglogistic_nll_shared,
  start = list(
    shape = 2,
    scale = median(times_combined)
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    shape = 0.001,
    scale = 0.001
  )
)

summary(loglogistic_fit_shared)

coef(loglogistic_fit_shared)

loglogistic_fit_shared@details$convergence
```
# Calculate the liklihood-ratio statistic
```{r}
# Log-likelihood under the null hypothesis
LL_null <- as.numeric(
  logLik(loglogistic_fit_shared)
)

# Log-likelihood under the alternative hypothesis
LL_alt <-
  as.numeric(logLik(loglogistic_fit)) +
  as.numeric(logLik(loglogistic_fit_viro))

# Likelihood-ratio statistic
LR <- 2 * (LL_alt - LL_null)

# Difference in parameter count: 4 - 2 = 2
df <- 2

# P-value
p_value <- pchisq(
  LR,
  df = df,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  LL_null = LL_null,
  LL_alt = LL_alt,
  LR = LR,
  df = df,
  p_value = p_value
)
```
